overall: Tomorrow (Friday, June 26) in Los Angeles will be a mild, marine-influenced day with patchy fog clearing by late morning, giving way to partly sunny skies. Expect a high near 70-72°F under continued southwest/south-southwest onshore flow of 5-10 mph. No tropical or severe weather threats are relevant to LA — the Phoenix Extreme Heat Warning and San Diego beach hazards are localized to those regions.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is reasonably tight on the top bucket (72-73°F), with ECMWF, GFS, HRRR, and Weather.com all selecting it as the most likely range; however, there is notable spread in expected values — ECMWF and HRRR cluster near 72.4°F, GFS runs warmer at 76.3°F, and NBM is an outlier on the cool side at 66.9°F, suggesting some uncertainty in how strongly the marine layer erodes through the afternoon.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble model points to a TMAX of approximately 71.6°F, well-supported by ECMWF and HRRR at ~72.4°F and yesterday's observed high of 72.0°F, giving high consistency with the 72-73°F top bucket (28.9% probability, Tier 1 confidence with an 8.1-point gap over the next bucket). The active market bucket to target is 72-73°F on the even set or 73-74°F on the odd set; the onshore marine influence and lingering fog should cap any afternoon warming, making a surge toward the GFS's warmer 76°F scenario unlikely.
